caption:
Is it your offer, or is it your traffic?

There is one test and it takes about a minute: look at the people who already said no.

If the WRONG people are saying no — people who were never going to buy, wrong budget, wrong problem, wrong city — that is a traffic problem. You are reaching the wrong room.

If the RIGHT people are saying no — your exact customer, with the budget and the problem — that is an offer problem. The room is right and the pitch is wrong.

This matters because the fixes have nothing in common. Traffic problems get fixed with targeting and creative. Offer problems get fixed with what you promise and what you charge.

And spending more only helps the first one. Running more traffic at a broken offer just buys you a bigger sample of no.
